draft.title: Cultural diffusion
card: Cultural diffusion is the spread of ideas, languages, foods, beliefs and other practices from one place or group to another. A practice that spreads often changes as it is taken up in a new place.
Trade
People who buy and sell across distances bring products and the practices tied to them. Traders carried spices, and with them cooking methods and words.
Migration
People who move to a new place bring their language, food, music and customs with them. These can then be shared with the people already living there.
Media
Television, film, music and the internet carry ideas to many people at once, without anyone having to travel. A song or trend can reach distant places in a day.
draft.remember: Culture spreads when goods, people and media carry it from place to place.

a.q: Families from Vietnam settle in Sydney and open bakeries selling banh mi. Neighbours begin to buy and cook it. Which process is mainly at work?
opts: Cultural diffusion through migration
Cultural diffusion through trade
Cultural diffusion through media
A shift in a country's development level
a.why: People moved to a new place and brought a food practice with them, which others then took up. That is diffusion through migration. Trade is tempting because bakeries sell food, but the practice arrived with the people, not with goods shipped from far away.
a.clue: What moved to Sydney: goods, people or broadcasts?

b.q: A dance challenge begins in South Korea and, within days, teenagers in Perth are copying it after watching clips on their phones. No one has travelled. What best describes this?
opts: Diffusion through media, as ideas spread without travel
Diffusion through migration, as dancers moved to Perth
Diffusion through trade, as dance products were sold
No diffusion, as nobody moved between the two places
b.why: Online clips carried the practice to Perth, so this is diffusion through media. The last option is tempting but wrong: the card says media can spread ideas without anyone travelling, so movement of people is not needed.
b.clue: Think about what carried the dance to Perth.

b.best: Diffusion through media, as ideas spread without travel

problems.detail: Why (b) points to 'the last option' by position, but options are shown in random order, so the reference may not match. Its reasoning ('movement of people is not needed') actually answers the 'No diffusion, as nobody moved' option, not the migration option. Name the distractor by its content instead.

The stem says 'No one has travelled' and the right option echoes it with 'as ideas spread without travel'. A student can match the wording without knowing the idea. The migration option is also ruled out by the stem itself.
